subject: english
question: Sofia’s exact words are “My kite has a blue tail.” Which sentence quotes those words directly?
audio_prompt: Sofia’s exact words are “My kite has a blue tail.” Which sentence quotes those words directly?

answers.text: Sofia said, “My kite has a blue tail.”
Sofia said that her kite had a blue tail.
Sofia said, “Your kite has a blue tail.”
Sofia said that the blue-tailed kite belonged to her.

explanation.summary: The words inside the quotation marks match Sofia’s actual words, including My. The other reports may retell the idea, but do not quote these exact words.
explanation.hint: Compare the words inside the marks with the original.

subject: english
question: Read: “Eli said that his painting was unfinished.” How is Eli’s message presented?
audio_prompt: Read: “Eli said that his painting was unfinished.” How is Eli’s message presented?

answers.text: As Eli’s exact words inside quotation marks
As reported speech in the narrator’s sentence
As a direct question addressed to Eli
As the narrator’s own opinion without a named speaker

explanation.summary: Said that introduces a report of Eli’s message. It does not give his exact original wording.
explanation.hint: Notice who reports the message and whether exact words are quoted.

subject: english
question: Mara says, “I need a ruler.” Sam tells a teacher what Mara needs. Which report keeps the right person?
audio_prompt: Mara says, “I need a ruler.” Sam tells a teacher what Mara needs. Which report keeps the right person?

answers.text: Sam reports that he needs a ruler.
Sam reports that the teacher needs a ruler.
Sam reports that Mara needs a ruler.
Sam reports that Mara has lent someone a ruler.

explanation.summary: I refers to Mara in the original. Sam must keep Mara as the person needing the ruler.
explanation.hint: Ask who I refers to in the original.

subject: english
question: The coach’s exact words were “We kept trying until the final whistle.” A team scrapbook wants to keep the coach’s wording. Which choice fits?
audio_prompt: The coach’s exact words were “We kept trying until the final whistle.” A team scrapbook wants to keep the coach’s wording. Which choice fits?

answers.text: The coach said that the team had continued trying.
The coach said, “We won at the final whistle.”
The coach promised that the team would win next time.
The coach said, “We kept trying until the final whistle.”

explanation.summary: Direct quotation preserves the coach’s actual wording. A summary serves another purpose; winning and a promise were not stated.
explanation.hint: Keep both the meaning and the exact words.

subject: english
question: A visitor says, “The pond is beside the library.” Which sentence reports the message without quoting it?
audio_prompt: A visitor says, “The pond is beside the library.” Which sentence reports the message without quoting it?

answers.text: The visitor said that the pond was beside the library.
The visitor said, “The pond is beside the library.”
“The pond is beside the library,” said the visitor.
The visitor said that the library was inside the pond.

explanation.summary: The reported version names the visitor and retells the location in the reporter’s sentence. The two quoted versions use direct speech.
explanation.hint: Look for a faithful retelling without quoted exact words.

subject: english
question: A meeting has many spoken turns. You only need a short record of the decision: everyone agreed to meet at noon. Which form suits that purpose?
audio_prompt: A meeting has many spoken turns. You only need a short record of the decision: everyone agreed to meet at noon. Which form suits that purpose?

answers.text: “Everyone said exactly these words: We all agree to noon.”
The group agreed to meet at noon.
The group had a very long discussion about meeting.
Each speaker’s full conversation, including greetings and unrelated details.

explanation.summary: A concise report records the decision. The prompt supplies a summary, so it does not justify inventing an exact quotation.
explanation.hint: Keep the known decision without inventing wording.

subject: english
question: Asha’s exact words are “I might bring my camera.” Which report keeps the uncertainty?
audio_prompt: Asha’s exact words are “I might bring my camera.” Which report keeps the uncertainty?

answers.text: Asha promised to bring her camera.
Asha said that she would definitely bring her camera.
Asha said that she might bring her camera.
Asha said that she could not bring her camera.

explanation.summary: Might leaves the plan uncertain. A promise, definite statement or refusal changes the message.
explanation.hint: Keep might rather than strengthening the plan.

subject: english
question: Noah says to Ruby, “Your drawing is clear.” Ruby immediately tells a friend what Noah said. Which report from Ruby keeps whose drawing it is?
audio_prompt: Noah says to Ruby, “Your drawing is clear.” Ruby immediately tells a friend what Noah said. Which report from Ruby keeps whose drawing it is?

answers.text: Noah said that his drawing is clear.
Noah said that your drawing is clear.
Noah said that his drawing is clearer than mine.
Noah said that my drawing is clear.

explanation.summary: Noah’s your points to Ruby. When Ruby reports it, my still refers to Ruby’s drawing.
explanation.hint: Track the speaker and the listener.

subject: english
question: On Tuesday morning, Leila says, “We leave tomorrow.” On Wednesday, Ben reports her plan and names the departure day. Which report keeps the intended day?
audio_prompt: On Tuesday morning, Leila says, “We leave tomorrow.” On Wednesday, Ben reports her plan and names the departure day. Which report keeps the intended day?

answers.text: Leila said that the group would leave on Wednesday.
Leila said that the group would leave on Thursday.
Leila said that the group had left on Monday.
Leila said that the group would leave every Tuesday.

explanation.summary: Tomorrow on Tuesday refers to Wednesday. Naming the day avoids shifting the trip to Thursday when Ben reports it.
explanation.hint: Anchor tomorrow to the original speaking day.

subject: english
question: At 9 am on Monday, Omar says, “The club meets today.” At 10 am that same Monday, Priya reports this while the meeting is still ahead. Which statement about today is correct?
audio_prompt: At 9 am on Monday, Omar says, “The club meets today.” At 10 am that same Monday, Priya reports this while the meeting is still ahead. Which statement about today is correct?

answers.text: Today must become tomorrow because the speaker changed.
Today can still refer to Monday in Priya’s report.
Today must refer to Sunday in every report.
Today cannot be used in any reported speech.

explanation.summary: Both speaking moments are on Monday. Time expressions change when the reference requires it, not simply because speech is reported.
explanation.hint: Check whether the reporting day changed.

subject: english
question: A teacher says, “A square has four sides.” Later, Ava reports this continuing fact: “The teacher said that a square has four sides.” What is accurate about Ava’s use of has?
audio_prompt: A teacher says, “A square has four sides.” Later, Ava reports this continuing fact: “The teacher said that a square has four sides.” What is accurate about Ava’s use of has?

answers.text: Has must become had simply because the message is reported.
Has shows that Ava is quoting the teacher’s exact whole sentence.
Has can remain present because the reported fact still holds.
Has can remain only if Ava, rather than the teacher, discovered the fact.

explanation.summary: A continuing fact can stay in the present tense in reported speech. A report does not always need tense backshift.
explanation.hint: Is the statement still true at the time of the report?

subject: english
question: Tane’s exact words are “I finished the model.” Which report wrongly changes who completed it?
audio_prompt: Tane’s exact words are “I finished the model.” Which report wrongly changes who completed it?

answers.text: Tane said that he had finished the model.
Tane reported finishing the model.
Tane said that the model was finished by him.
Tane said that the reporter had finished the model.

explanation.summary: The original attributes the work to Tane. Making the reporter the maker changes that information.
explanation.hint: Keep the original doer of the action.

subject: english
question: An interviewer records these exact words from a gardener: “The tiny shoots looked like green umbrellas.” Why might a magazine quote this sentence directly?
audio_prompt: An interviewer records these exact words from a gardener: “The tiny shoots looked like green umbrellas.” Why might a magazine quote this sentence directly?

answers.text: To preserve the gardener’s distinctive comparison and voice
To turn the gardener’s comparison into a measured fact
To make the reporter the person who spoke the words
To avoid showing who made the comparison

explanation.summary: The green-umbrellas comparison is memorable wording. A quotation keeps that voice while crediting the gardener.
explanation.hint: Think about what a summary might lose.

subject: english
question: A school notice needs the main message of a long talk: the art club starts at 3 pm in Room 2. Which report is most useful?
audio_prompt: A school notice needs the main message of a long talk: the art club starts at 3 pm in Room 2. Which report is most useful?

answers.text: The organiser said that there would be an art club somewhere.
The organiser said that the art club starts at 3 pm in Room 2.
The organiser said, “There were many interesting things in my talk.”
The organiser said that the art club had been cancelled.

explanation.summary: The report preserves the practical time and place without needing the full talk’s wording.
explanation.hint: Retain the details the notice reader needs.

subject: english
question: Luca speaks in a whisper: “Please close the window.” Which reporting verb adds a detail that the context actually supports?
audio_prompt: Luca speaks in a whisper: “Please close the window.” Which reporting verb adds a detail that the context actually supports?

answers.text: Luca shouted, “Please close the window.”
Luca promised, “Please close the window.”
Luca whispered, “Please close the window.”
Luca argued, “Please close the window.”

explanation.summary: Whispered suits the supplied quiet voice. The other verbs introduce an unsupported loudness, commitment or disagreement.
explanation.hint: Use only a speaking detail the context supports.

subject: english
question: A note only says: “Mina asked for another sheet of paper.” You do not know her exact words. What is the accurate way to include this in a report?
audio_prompt: A note only says: “Mina asked for another sheet of paper.” You do not know her exact words. What is the accurate way to include this in a report?

answers.text: Mina said, “Give me another sheet immediately.”
Mina said, “Could I please have a blue sheet?”
Mina said, “I have never had enough paper.”
Mina asked for another sheet of paper.

explanation.summary: A known summary supports a report. It does not support invented exact wording, colour or tone.
explanation.hint: Do you have exact words or only their meaning?

subject: english
question: On Friday, Jae said, “I will practise tomorrow.” On Monday, a reporter tells what Jae planned. Which named day belongs in the report?
audio_prompt: On Friday, Jae said, “I will practise tomorrow.” On Monday, a reporter tells what Jae planned. Which named day belongs in the report?

answers.text: Jae said that he would practise on Saturday.
Jae said that he would practise on Tuesday.
Jae said that he would practise on Thursday.
Jae said that he would practise every Monday.

explanation.summary: The original tomorrow follows Friday, so it means Saturday even though the report is made later.
explanation.hint: Use the day of the original speech.

subject: english
question: The exact statement is: Tara said, “Our class collected twelve cans.” Which report preserves the amount and the group?
audio_prompt: The exact statement is: Tara said, “Our class collected twelve cans.” Which report preserves the amount and the group?

answers.text: Tara said that she alone had collected twelve cans.
Tara said that her class had collected twelve cans.
Tara said that her class had collected twenty cans.
Tara said that every class had collected twelve cans.

explanation.summary: Our class becomes her class when Tara’s words are reported by another person. The amount remains twelve.
explanation.hint: Check both who and how many.

subject: english
question: A report reads, “Max promised to return the book.” Which original statement best supports the word promised?
audio_prompt: A report reads, “Max promised to return the book.” Which original statement best supports the word promised?

answers.text: “I might return the book,” Max said.
“I wonder who borrowed the book,” Max said.
“I promise I will return the book,” Max said.
“Someone else returned the book,” Max said.

explanation.summary: An explicit promise supports the reporting verb. Possibility, wondering and another person’s action do not.
explanation.hint: What commitment does the original speaker make?

subject: english
question: Nia said, “I am not ready.” Which report keeps the negative meaning?
audio_prompt: Nia said, “I am not ready.” Which report keeps the negative meaning?

answers.text: Nia said that she was ready.
Nia said that everyone was not ready.
Nia said that she would never be ready.
Nia said that she was not ready.

explanation.summary: Not ready preserves Nia’s statement. Removing not, widening it to everyone or adding never changes the claim.
explanation.hint: Keep the scope and strength of not.

subject: english
question: A journalist has the exact statement “The journey was tiring but exciting,” from a walker. Which sentence accurately combines a report with a short exact quotation?
audio_prompt: A journalist has the exact statement “The journey was tiring but exciting,” from a walker. Which sentence accurately combines a report with a short exact quotation?

answers.text: The walker described the journey as “tiring but exciting”.
The walker described the journey as “easy but exciting”.
The walker described everyone’s journeys as “tiring but exciting”.
The walker promised that the next journey would be “tiring but exciting”.

explanation.summary: The quoted phrase is exact, and the reported frame keeps its speaker and subject. A report may include a clearly marked exact phrase.
explanation.hint: Check the quoted phrase and its surrounding claim.

subject: english
question: A character says, “Don’t touch the wet paint!” A story writer wants readers to hear the urgent warning. Which choice best preserves that spoken moment?
audio_prompt: A character says, “Don’t touch the wet paint!” A story writer wants readers to hear the urgent warning. Which choice best preserves that spoken moment?

answers.text: The character mentioned that paint existed.
“Don’t touch the wet paint!” the character called.
The character said, “Please repaint the wall next week.”
The character wondered whether anyone liked painting.

explanation.summary: The exact warning lets the reader hear the character’s urgency. The other versions omit or change the warning.
explanation.hint: Preserve the message and its force for this story moment.

subject: english
question: At the school gate, Hana says to Joel, “I left my bag here.” Later, at home, Joel tells his family where Hana left it. Which report avoids changing the location?
audio_prompt: At the school gate, Hana says to Joel, “I left my bag here.” Later, at home, Joel tells his family where Hana left it. Which report avoids changing the location?

answers.text: Hana said that she had left her bag here at our home.
Hana said that I had left my bag at the school gate.
Hana said that she had left her bag at the school gate.
Hana said that she had found Joel’s bag at home.

explanation.summary: Here meant the school gate when Hana spoke. Naming that place keeps the location clear after Joel moves home.
explanation.hint: Anchor here to the original speaking place.

subject: english
question: You are at the library with Finn. Finn says, “The display is here.” You immediately tell another friend beside you what he said. Must here change to there?
audio_prompt: You are at the library with Finn. Finn says, “The display is here.” You immediately tell another friend beside you what he said. Must here change to there?

answers.text: Yes; all reported speech must use there.
Yes; a different listener always changes the physical location.
No; here must always stay even if the reporter later leaves.
No; here can still mean the same library location.

explanation.summary: The location has not changed in this context. A later report from another place may need different wording.
explanation.hint: Check the reporter’s location, not just the form of speech.

subject: english
question: Imogen says, “We need two volunteers.” Her group is Imogen and two classmates. A teacher reports this to another class. Which report keeps the group’s need?
audio_prompt: Imogen says, “We need two volunteers.” Her group is Imogen and two classmates. A teacher reports this to another class. Which report keeps the group’s need?

answers.text: Imogen said that her group needed two volunteers.
Imogen said that only she needed two volunteers.
Imogen said that the volunteers needed two groups.
Imogen said that the whole school needed twenty volunteers.

explanation.summary: We refers to the identified group. Reporting should preserve that group and the number requested.
explanation.hint: Identify the people included in we.

subject: english
question: Read this pair: A: “The bridge is slippery,” said the guide. B: The guide warned that the bridge was slippery. Which statement compares the forms accurately?
audio_prompt: Read this pair: A: “The bridge is slippery,” said the guide. B: The guide warned that the bridge was slippery. Which statement compares the forms accurately?

answers.text: A gives only a summary; B reproduces exact words in quotation marks.
A gives the guide’s words directly; B reports the warning in the writer’s sentence.
Both must be the guide’s exact original words.
B proves the guide shouted, while A proves the guide whispered.

explanation.summary: The quotation in A is presented as exact speech. B integrates the warning into a report, without proving volume.
explanation.hint: Look for exact quoted words versus a reported message.

subject: english
question: A report says, “Zara admitted that she had moved the marker.” The only source is Zara calmly saying, “I moved the marker.” Why might said be a more careful choice than admitted?
audio_prompt: A report says, “Zara admitted that she had moved the marker.” The only source is Zara calmly saying, “I moved the marker.” Why might said be a more careful choice than admitted?

answers.text: Said would make the marker belong to a different person.
Admitted means the reporter knows Zara’s exact tone and reason.
Admitted may suggest acknowledging something wrong, which the source does not establish.
Said can only be used with direct quotations.

explanation.summary: Reporting verbs can add interpretation. A neutral said avoids implying wrongdoing without evidence.
explanation.hint: Does the reporting verb add a judgement not in the source?

subject: english
question: The exact words are “We could meet after lunch,” said the organiser. Which report wrongly turns a suggestion into a fixed decision?
audio_prompt: The exact words are “We could meet after lunch,” said the organiser. Which report wrongly turns a suggestion into a fixed decision?

answers.text: The organiser suggested meeting after lunch.
The organiser said that they could meet after lunch.
The organiser put forward after lunch as a possible meeting time.
The organiser decided that everyone would meet after lunch.

explanation.summary: Could offers a possibility. Decided that everyone would makes it a settled plan that was not stated.
explanation.hint: Keep a possibility separate from a decision.

subject: english
question: An account says, “Leo said that his team was tired.” Which conclusion is justified?
audio_prompt: An account says, “Leo said that his team was tired.” Which conclusion is justified?

answers.text: The account reports Leo’s message, but not necessarily his exact words.
Leo must have said the exact words “his team was tired”.
The reporter must have been a member of Leo’s team.
The team must have stopped playing immediately.

explanation.summary: A reported message does not reveal the speaker’s exact phrasing or actions beyond the stated content.
explanation.hint: Distinguish the message from words or events not supplied.

subject: english
question: A reporter changes “I prefer the red design” into “Ari said that everyone preferred the red design.” What has changed incorrectly?
audio_prompt: A reporter changes “I prefer the red design” into “Ari said that everyone preferred the red design.” What has changed incorrectly?

answers.text: A preference has been kept as one person’s view.
One person’s preference has become everyone’s preference.
The colour red has been changed to blue.
The report has kept I referring to the reporter.

explanation.summary: I gives Ari’s own view. Everyone widens it to a group without evidence.
explanation.hint: Check whose viewpoint the report represents.

subject: english
question: On Wednesday, Mei says, “The show is today.” On Friday, a reporter names the show day in a past account. Which wording preserves the original day?
audio_prompt: On Wednesday, Mei says, “The show is today.” On Friday, a reporter names the show day in a past account. Which wording preserves the original day?

answers.text: Mei said that the show was on Friday.
Mei said that the show would be on Saturday.
Mei said that the show was on Wednesday.
Mei said that the show happened every day.

explanation.summary: Today in the original referred to Wednesday. Reporting later should not shift the show to the reporter’s today.
explanation.hint: Use the original speaking date.

subject: english
question: Amir says, “I can lend you my spare pencil.” He is speaking to Jess. Jess immediately reports the offer to a teacher. Which version preserves the owner and receiver?
audio_prompt: Amir says, “I can lend you my spare pencil.” He is speaking to Jess. Jess immediately reports the offer to a teacher. Which version preserves the owner and receiver?

answers.text: Amir said that I could lend him my spare pencil.
Amir said that the teacher could lend me a pencil.
Amir said that he had borrowed Jess’s only pencil.
Amir said that he could lend me his spare pencil.

explanation.summary: Amir owns the spare pencil; Jess is the offered receiver. In Jess’s report, me still names Jess.
explanation.hint: Track I, you and my through the change of speaker.

subject: english
question: A class newsletter contains an exact quotation but credits it to the wrong child. The words themselves are unchanged. What still needs correcting?
audio_prompt: A class newsletter contains an exact quotation but credits it to the wrong child. The words themselves are unchanged. What still needs correcting?

answers.text: The named speaker, so the words are attributed accurately.
The wording inside the quotation must change to suit the person incorrectly named.
The report should omit every speaker name even though the true speaker is known.
The incorrect name can stay as long as the quotation’s wording is exact.

explanation.summary: A responsible quotation needs both accurate words and accurate attribution. Exact wording alone is not enough.
explanation.hint: Ask whose words they are.

subject: english
question: An artist’s exact words are “The stripes remind me of rain.” A writer changes stripes to spots inside the quotation without saying so. Why is that a problem?
audio_prompt: An artist’s exact words are “The stripes remind me of rain.” A writer changes stripes to spots inside the quotation without saying so. Why is that a problem?

answers.text: The substitution is acceptable inside a direct quote because stripes and spots are both patterns.
The quotation no longer preserves the artist’s actual words and image.
Only the speaker’s name needs to match; the writer may freely change words inside the quote.
Changing the image makes the quotation a more precise record of the artist’s original wording.

explanation.summary: Direct quotation should not silently change meaningful wording. A writer can paraphrase accurately outside quotation marks instead.
explanation.hint: Compare the image in the original and the changed version.

subject: english
question: A report about a trip says, “The leader said that the bus would leave at nine.” Which question cannot be answered from this report alone?
audio_prompt: A report about a trip says, “The leader said that the bus would leave at nine.” Which question cannot be answered from this report alone?

answers.text: Who gave the message?
What transport was mentioned?
What exact sentence did the leader speak?
What leaving time was reported?

explanation.summary: The report gives the leader, bus and time, but it does not reproduce an exact original sentence.
explanation.hint: What does a summary leave unknown?

subject: english
question: A cook says, “Add one spoon of oil, then stir.” Which short reported instruction preserves both the amount and the order?
audio_prompt: A cook says, “Add one spoon of oil, then stir.” Which short reported instruction preserves both the amount and the order?

answers.text: The cook told us to stir and then add two spoons of oil.
The cook told us to leave out the oil and keep stirring.
The cook told us to add oil without saying how much or when to stir.
The cook told us to add one spoon of oil and then stir.

explanation.summary: The report keeps one spoon and adding before stirring. Concision must not remove essential instructions.
explanation.hint: Check the quantity and the sequence.

subject: english
question: A reporter writes, “Ella said that she was nervous.” The original was “I feel a little nervous,” Ella said. Which report keeps the degree of feeling more precisely?
audio_prompt: A reporter writes, “Ella said that she was nervous.” The original was “I feel a little nervous,” Ella said. Which report keeps the degree of feeling more precisely?

answers.text: Ella said that she felt a little nervous.
Ella said that she was terrified.
Ella said that everyone felt nervous.
Ella said that she never felt nervous.

explanation.summary: A little keeps the mild degree of nervousness. Terrified exaggerates it; the other versions change scope or meaning.
explanation.hint: Preserve small words that show strength.

subject: english
question: A story uses the quotation “Wait for me!” followed by a paragraph reporting a longer discussion about the route. Why might the writer use both forms?
audio_prompt: A story uses the quotation “Wait for me!” followed by a paragraph reporting a longer discussion about the route. Why might the writer use both forms?

answers.text: A report is only allowed after a quotation in every story.
The quotation captures a short spoken moment; the report can summarise the longer discussion.
The quotation proves every word of the discussion was recorded.
The writer must use one form because the two cannot appear together.

explanation.summary: Writers can combine direct and reported speech for different purposes within one text.
explanation.hint: Match each form to the job it does here.

subject: english
question: Ava reports her own earlier words. At lunch she said, “I need more time.” Later she tells the teacher, “I said that I needed more time.” Why does I stay?
audio_prompt: Ava reports her own earlier words. At lunch she said, “I need more time.” Later she tells the teacher, “I said that I needed more time.” Why does I stay?

answers.text: I must stay in every report, whoever is speaking.
Needed means a different person needs the time.
Ava is both the original speaker and the person reporting her own message.
The quotation marks around the whole example prove it is not a report.

explanation.summary: Pronouns depend on viewpoint. Ava can use I in her own report because it still points to Ava.
explanation.hint: Is the original speaker also the reporter?

subject: english
question: The exact message is: “I have two tickets, but one is for my brother,” said Jay. A friend reports, “Jay said he had two spare tickets for us.” What was lost?
audio_prompt: The exact message is: “I have two tickets, but one is for my brother,” said Jay. A friend reports, “Jay said he had two spare tickets for us.” What was lost?

answers.text: The information that Jay has tickets at all.
The name of the person who spoke.
The fact that the message is about a past holiday.
The limit that one ticket is for Jay’s brother.

explanation.summary: The original does not offer both tickets to the friend. The omitted limit changes what the listener can assume.
explanation.hint: Keep details that limit the message.

subject: english
question: Invent one sentence that a fictional gardener could say about a plant. Write it as a direct quotation with the gardener named. Then report the same message in another person’s sentence and explain one change.
audio_prompt: Invent one sentence that a fictional gardener could say about a plant. Write it as a direct quotation with the gardener named. Then report the same message in another person’s sentence and explain one change.
model_answer: Mina said, “My sunflower is taller than the fence.” Ben reported that Mina’s sunflower was taller than the fence. My becomes Mina’s because Ben is reporting her plant.
acceptance_note: Require an actual invented utterance, named speaker, exact words inside the direct quote, a faithful report and one justified viewpoint/wording change. Accept grammatically valid present or past reporting where context permits.
response_instructions: Write or dictate the actual quotation, report and explanation requested. You may use your usual communication support. An adult checks the completed work against the guidance.
completion_label: My completed work is ready for an adult to check.

explanation.summary: Mina said, “My sunflower is taller than the fence.” Ben reported that Mina’s sunflower was taller than the fence. My becomes Mina’s because Ben is reporting her plant.
explanation.hint: Keep the plant, its detail and its speaker the same.

subject: english
question: The supplied exact words are “I might bring three brushes,” said Theo. Write a reported version for a teacher, then explain why you should not use promised.
audio_prompt: The supplied exact words are “I might bring three brushes,” said Theo. Write a reported version for a teacher, then explain why you should not use promised.
model_answer: Theo said that he might bring three brushes. Promised would make an uncertain possibility into a commitment.
acceptance_note: Require Theo, three brushes and might or an equivalent uncertainty preserved. Explanation must distinguish possibility from promise. Accept Theo repeated instead of he.
response_instructions: Write or dictate the actual quotation, report and explanation requested. You may use your usual communication support. An adult checks the completed work against the guidance.
completion_label: My completed work is ready for an adult to check.

explanation.summary: Theo said that he might bring three brushes. Promised would make an uncertain possibility into a commitment.
explanation.hint: Check certainty as well as objects and numbers.

subject: english
question: On Monday, Suri says, “Our group will visit tomorrow.” On Thursday, write a report naming the planned visiting day rather than using tomorrow. Explain how you chose the day.
audio_prompt: On Monday, Suri says, “Our group will visit tomorrow.” On Thursday, write a report naming the planned visiting day rather than using tomorrow. Explain how you chose the day.
model_answer: Suri said that her group would visit on Tuesday. Tomorrow meant the day after Monday, so it referred to Tuesday.
acceptance_note: Require Suri’s group, Tuesday and a planned visit rather than claiming the visit definitely occurred. Explain the original-day reference. Accept other grammatical reporting verbs without extra certainty.
response_instructions: Write or dictate the actual quotation, report and explanation requested. You may use your usual communication support. An adult checks the completed work against the guidance.
completion_label: My completed work is ready for an adult to check.

explanation.summary: Suri said that her group would visit on Tuesday. Tomorrow meant the day after Monday, so it referred to Tuesday.
explanation.hint: Anchor the time word to when Suri spoke.

subject: english
question: A brief note says only: “The caretaker asked the class to leave the doorway clear.” Write a faithful reported sentence and explain why you cannot supply an exact quotation from this note alone.
audio_prompt: A brief note says only: “The caretaker asked the class to leave the doorway clear.” Write a faithful reported sentence and explain why you cannot supply an exact quotation from this note alone.
model_answer: The caretaker asked the class to keep the doorway clear. The note gives the message but not the caretaker’s exact words, so I should not invent a quotation.
acceptance_note: Require the caretaker, class and clear doorway retained, plus the exact-wording limitation. No child needs to contact a real caretaker or record anyone.
